correctness.rationale: The exact iff condition is proved for n>=4 and 1/n<r<1/(n-1) using the cycle/interval-nerve dichotomy. The ordered gap density carries the correct (n-1)! label factor. The complement-deficit simplex Jacobian and Dirichlet covariance produce exact probability, vanishing order-h correction, and explicit order-h^2 Hessian coefficient. Positive C3 f yields uniform Taylor remainder and positive normalization. Uniform conditional density convergence proves the product Dirichlet total-variation limit. AM-GM, Jensen and Chebyshev establish strict harmonic n-divisibility. An executed stand-alone numerical checker corroborates 800 topological cases, 24 harmonic cases and two second-order families; not used to infer the general theorem.

originality.rationale: Primary full text of Park arXiv:2610.26366 gives an exact UNIFORM random circle homotopy law and credits Stevens for the first circle window. The fixed n positive nonuniform density asymptotic, conditional near-regular Dirichlet shape, disappearance of the first relative correction and sharp harmonic resonance are not asserted there. Adamaszek--Adams proves deterministic homotopy for arbitrary sets, not the probability/conditional claims. Lim studies uniform Cech topology. Jewell--Romano (1982) explicitly treats general nonuniform arc coverage and may provide a stronger exact probability identity, but an exact coverage probability alone is not the conditional-shape/resonance theorem; its inaccessible full text is a real residual originality risk, not falsely dismissed. Huesler (1988) concerns large-n spacings with vanishing density. Actual indexed and textual searches found no direct or implied covering conjunction; lack of a hit is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: A natural first topological loop onset in finite-sample Rips complexes is quantified under nonuniform sampling. The limit identifies the geometry of rare near-regular configurations, a centered second-order density response, and a strict n-divisibility harmonic resonance affecting sampling bias. These are motivated structural laws for a natural topological probability, not an arbitrary calculation; the general nonuniform gap integral alone is not used as the value basis.
